title: Caveat Emptor — No Mandatory Seller Disclosure
description: Wyoming is one of the few remaining caveat emptor states for residential real estate. Wyoming has no statutory requirement for sellers to complete a property condition disclosure form. Buyers bear the responsibility to inspect and investigate property conditions. However, sellers may not actively conceal known defects or make fraudulent misrepresentations. The Wyoming Association of Realtors offers a voluntary Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form, but it is not legally mandated.

required_actions.note: No statutory disclosure required. Voluntary disclosure form recommended as best practice. Buyers should conduct thorough independent inspections.

citations: Caveat emptor applies — no WY statute mandates seller disclosure
Barnette v. Doyle, 2009 WY 90 (reaffirming no duty to disclose absent special relationship)

metadata.note: Wyoming is a caveat emptor state. One of approximately 4 US states with no mandatory residential seller disclosure form.

title: Agency Disclosure and Brokerage Relationships
description: Wyoming requires real estate licensees to disclose their agency relationship in writing prior to engaging in any act that requires a real estate license. Wyoming recognizes buyer agency, seller agency, dual agency (with written consent), and disclosed limited agency. The Wyoming Real Estate Commission requires use of the Brokerage Disclosure Form.

required_actions.note: Must be provided before any act requiring a license. Dual agency requires written informed consent of both parties.

title: Closing Practice — Title Company/Escrow
description: Wyoming is not an attorney-close state. Closings are typically conducted by title companies or escrow agents. Attorney involvement is optional. Wyoming uses mortgage instruments for secured real estate transactions. Title insurance is standard practice.

required_actions.note: Title company or escrow agent handles closing. Attorney optional.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. This is one of the few mandatory disclosures in Wyoming real estate transactions. Sellers must provide the EPA pamphlet and allow a 10-day inspection contingency.

title: Real Estate Advertising Compliance
description: Wyoming Real Estate Commission rules require that all real estate advertising include the licensed name of the brokerage firm. Internet advertising must include the firm name and state of licensure. All advertising must be truthful and not misleading under Wyoming Real Estate Commission Chapter 2 rules.

required_actions.note: All ads must include firm name as licensed. Internet ads must include firm name and state.
